findings.highlight: It’s eleven o’clock
findings.evidenceJa: 午後十一時を過ぎ
findings.governingReading: it is past eleven at night
findings.explanation: The English shifts the time backward from after eleven to exactly eleven.

findings.highlight: the town is going to sleep
findings.evidenceJa: 町は完全に眠りについた
findings.governingReading: the town has fallen completely asleep
findings.explanation: A completed, total stillness becomes an ongoing transition.

findings.highlight: we shouldn’t fight them
findings.evidenceJa: 手は出すな
findings.governingReading: do not make a move against that troublesome opponent
findings.explanation: The English narrows Rin’s broader prohibition on engaging or interfering to fighting.

findings.highlight: avoid careless attacks
findings.evidenceJa: 軽はずみな侵攻は避けたい
findings.governingReading: avoid a rash incursion
findings.explanation: Saber’s warning about entering the temple’s ground becomes generic plural attacks.

findings.highlight: put off attacking the Ryuudou Temple until we get more information
findings.evidenceJa: 柳洞寺はもう少し情報を得てから探りを入れる
findings.governingReading: investigate or probe Ryuudou Temple after obtaining more information
findings.explanation: Shirou proposes delaying reconnaissance; mirror moon turns the later action into an attack.

findings.highlight: when we don’t know anything about our enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 相手がどのサーヴァントのマスターかも知らないうちに
findings.governingReading: before knowing which Servant the opponent is Master of
findings.explanation: A specific tactical information gap is generalized into knowing nothing about the enemy.

findings.highlight: A Master that would set up his base in the Ryuudou Temple would not readily reveal his identity. If we are to quickly defeat him, we must face them
findings.evidenceJa: マスターならば、おいそれと正体を明かさないでしょう
findings.governingReading: such a Master would not readily reveal their identity, so an early decision requires breaking through by force
findings.explanation: The English oscillates between “him” and “them” for one Master, obscuring Saber’s single target.

findings.highlight: Saber is determined
findings.evidenceJa: きっぱりと断言する
findings.governingReading: inactive source narration: she declares it flatly
findings.explanation: mirror moon activates a semicolon-commented narration line absent from the active Japanese scene and also changes decisive speech into an internal state.

findings.highlight: we have to do something
findings.evidenceJa: 一日でも早く止めなくてはいけない
findings.governingReading: we must stop the culprit even one day sooner
findings.explanation: The English replaces stopping the coma attacks as soon as possible with unspecified action.

findings.highlight: I’d like to do more, but I can’t support you
findings.evidenceJa: 情けないが、俺にはセイバーの援護ができない
findings.governingReading: it is pathetic, but Shirou cannot support Saber
findings.explanation: Shirou’s shame over incapacity becomes an unsupported claim that he would like to do more.

findings.highlight: I can’t allow Saber to get hurt, just like the fight with Berserker
findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーの時のように、セイバーだけを傷つける事はできない
findings.governingReading: he cannot let Saber alone be hurt as she was against Berserker
findings.explanation: The English removes the crucial “alone” and makes the Berserker fight sound like a model for preventing injury rather than the prior failure he refuses to repeat.

findings.highlight: even if the enemy is weak
findings.evidenceJa: 万一倒せる相手が出てきても
findings.governingReading: even if an opponent they can defeat should appear
findings.explanation: Defeatability in their actual circumstances is replaced by an assertion that the enemy is weak.

findings.highlight: I want to avoid heading into a minefield
findings.evidenceJa: 自分から地雷原につっこむような真似は避けたい
findings.governingReading: he wants to avoid doing anything like charging into a minefield of his own accord
findings.explanation: The English loses both the simile and Shirou’s emphasis on initiating the reckless charge himself.

findings.highlight: please warn me
findings.evidenceJa: そういう時は注意してくれると助かる
findings.governingReading: it would help if Saber cautioned him in such a case
findings.explanation: The English removes the condition tying Saber’s intervention to Shirou’s bad tactical judgment.

findings.highlight: That joke isn’t very Saber-like
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーにあるまじき冗談を聞いた気がする
findings.governingReading: he feels as though he heard a joke unworthy of or uncharacteristic for Saber
findings.explanation: A tentative impression becomes a flat characterization.

findings.highlight: It must be Fuji-nee’s influence
findings.evidenceJa: 藤ねえの影響なのか
findings.governingReading: perhaps it is Taiga’s influence
findings.explanation: Shirou’s question-like speculation is promoted into certainty.

findings.highlight: But putting that aside, Shirou… will Sakura be all right?
findings.evidenceJa: 私たちはともかく、桜は大丈夫なのですか
findings.governingReading: leaving Saber and Shirou themselves aside, is Sakura all right
findings.explanation: The English’s vague “that” removes the contrast between the pair going out and Sakura remaining ill.

findings.highlight: She seemed unusually distressed
findings.evidenceJa: あの苦しみようは尋常ではありませんでした
findings.governingReading: the way she was suffering was not normal
findings.explanation: Saber’s alarm at visibly abnormal suffering is softened to unusual distress.

findings.highlight: I didn’t see anything unusual when I took her temperature
findings.evidenceJa: 熱を計ってみたら大した事なかった
findings.governingReading: when he measured her fever, it was not serious
findings.explanation: A present but modest fever becomes an absence of any unusual measurement.

findings.highlight: I have to act like a Master now
findings.evidenceJa: ここからはマスターとしての時間だ
findings.governingReading: from here on, it is his time as a Master
findings.explanation: Shirou’s deliberate division between domestic concern and Master duty becomes performative imitation.

findings.highlight: The wind is blowing the overhead clouds
findings.evidenceJa: 風があるのか、上空の雲が速い
findings.governingReading: perhaps there is wind; the clouds high above are moving fast
findings.explanation: A tentative inference from fast clouds is stated as directly known wind.

findings.highlight: Lit by fading moonlight
findings.evidenceJa: 白々とした月が見え隠れする中
findings.governingReading: as the pale moon appears and disappears behind the clouds
findings.explanation: The English replaces intermittent visibility of the pale moon with moonlight fading.

findings.highlight: we start running towards enemy territory
findings.evidenceJa: マスターの潜む敵地へと走り出した
findings.governingReading: they run toward enemy ground where a Master lies hidden
findings.explanation: The destination remains generic enemy territory after the English removes the concealed Master who defines it.
